newsitem.title: INDIA: Mother Teresa stable but still not out of danger.
newsitem.headline: Mother Teresa stable but still not out of danger.

text.p: Doctors treating Mother Teresa said on Monday that the Roman Catholic missionary was not out of danger following heart surgery, but they were optimistic that she would recover.

"She is stable and we are very optimistic about her recovery," U.S. doctor Patricia Aubanel, a member of the medical team treating Mother Teresa, told reporters at Calcutta's B.M. Birla Heart Research Centre.

The 86-year-old Roman Catholic nun, known as the "Saint of the Gutters" for her devotion to the poor, destitute and dying, had surgery on Friday to clear two coronary artery blockages. She is also suffering kidney and lung problems.
"Mother is still not out of danger and complications still may happen, but doctors this morning are optimistic," a medical bulletin issued by the hospital said.
Aubanel said doctors were now concentrating on Mother Teresa's kidney and lung problems, which the U.S. expert called the main concerns.

D.P. Shetty, chief of the medical team treating the Nobel Prize winner, said on Sunday that Mother Teresa's heart pacemaker, fitted in 1989, had been reprogrammed to boost cardiac output to allow her kidneys to function better.
"It's too early to say when she will be released," Aubanel told reporters.
Mother Teresa, born of Albanian parents as Gonxhe Bojaxhi, was moved to the clinic last Tuesday after entering the nearby Woodlands Nursing Home on November 22.
